problem: Adjacent-channel crosstalk is defined as 'the wanted channel power divided by the leakage from the next channel', which is a ratio greater than 1 and therefore gives a positive dB value. The same sentence then says 'more negative is better', and Q6 and the exam traps also use negative dB. The definition contradicts its own sign convention and the standard textbook definition.
fix: Adjacent-channel crosstalk is the leakage power from the next channel divided by the wanted channel power, in dB; because the leakage is smaller, the value is negative and more negative is better (e.g. −30 dB is better than −20 dB).

problem: 'Total capacity is N × B per direction; do not multiply by N again for a duplex pair' is wrong as written. Counting both directions means multiplying by 2 (a factor of two), not by N; a student will copy 'multiply by N' into the exam.
fix: Total capacity is N × B per direction; multiply by 2 for a duplex pair only if the question says both directions are counted, and never multiply by N a second time.
